subject: [FinEx] Throughput sizing follow-up — tokens/sec, QPS, streaming
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos@finexpayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinEx discovery — perf targets and workload profile

Hi Carlos / Anita —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum: 

What I captured as FinEx goals:
- Latency SLO: 95th pct <= 300ms for single-turn chat generation (avg prompt ~120 tokens).
- Streaming required for customer-facing chat UI (progressive tokens).
- Target concurrency: 150 concurrent chat sessions during peak; baseline steady-state ~25 concurrent.
- Peak traffic pattern: short bursty spikes correlated with payroll windows (expected 10–15x baseline for ~10–20 minutes).
- Cost sensitivity: want to understand per-token unit economics across quantized model variants.

Immediate asks from our side: 
1) Can you share a simple workload export (CSV) with timestamped request counts and average prompt/response token lengths — sample of a week if available. File format stub attached (finex_workload_profile_v1.csv).
2) Confirm whether streaming must include token-level latency under 100ms or if chunked 200–300ms is acceptable.
3) Any existing SLA/contract language around peak handling we should be aware of.

Next steps: we’ll run a quick sizing pass and send a recommended instance/throughput profile and an initial cost estimate by Wed (21 Jul). Marissa will lead the sizing and include recommended batching + KV cache settings.

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: finex_workload_profile_v1.csv (CSV, 45KB)

Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finexpayments.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinEx discovery — perf targets and workload profile

Rafael —

Thanks, this looks good. I uploaded a 7-day export to the CSV you attached. Key notes:
- Baseline QPS: ~4 req/s (avg across 24h)
- Peak QPS: observed 45 req/s during payroll windows (two peaks per day)
- Avg prompt tokens: 120 tokens in, avg response tokens: 280 tokens
- Many sessions are single-turn, but ~30% are multi-turn (2–5 turns), which would benefit from KV cache reuse.
- Streaming: client expects progressive tokens; they prefer tight inter-token pacing but 200ms chunking is acceptable if it reduces cost.

I attached the CSV and added a short notes column. Let us know if you need different aggregation.
—Carlos
FinEx — Director, Platform Engineering

Attachment: finex_workload_profile_v1.csv (CSV, 62KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos@finexpayments.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinEx discovery — perf targets and workload profile

Thanks for the data, Carlos — uploaded successfully. Rafael / FinEx — initial sizing notes from my pass: 

Summary (ballpark for steady-state vs peak):
- Model assumption: 7B open-arch model quantized to 4-bit (FP16 equivalent perf improvements assumed via Redwood kernel optimizations).
- Steady-state (25 concurrent): ~1.2K tokens/sec system-wide; estimated 40 req/s effective throughput given batching opportunities (avg response 280 tokens).
- Peak (150 concurrent bursts): ~7K tokens/sec needed to keep 95p latency ~300ms assuming continuous batching; equals roughly 45–50 req/s sustained which matches Carlos’ observed peak QPS.
- Concurrency translation: 150 concurrent chat sessions with average response size ~280 tokens implies bursty CPU/GPU usage; recommend autoscaling headroom 1.5x for safety.

Streaming considerations:
- To deliver progressive tokens with <200ms user-visible pacing we recommend token-chunked streaming with 1–4 token groups; this slightly increases scheduling overhead but keeps UX smooth.

Proposed quick tests we’d like to run (can be done in hosted sandbox):
1) Synthetic burst test matching FinEx peak shape (45 req/s for 15 mins) to validate tail latency at 95p.
2) Multi-turn scenario with KV cache warm-up to measure per-turn latency improvements.

I’ll draft an initial Redwood recommendation PDF and a nominal cost estimate; Rafael — want to review before we send to FinEx.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
